what: Both attachments in a fold are READ_ONLY
why: Attaching an old trace for writing and detaching it runs a checkpoint; on 2 Nov that rewrote a 14.2 GiB trace to 18.1 GiB, filled the disk and failed
evidence: trace-store.mjs tryAttach; a scratch database grew 12,288 B to 536,576 B under a write attach and kept its bytes and WAL under a read-only one

what: A fold that leaves a trace behind records it in traces/left-behind.json and exits 1
why: One failed trace stopped every trace behind it from 31 Oct to 2 Nov, and the launcher ran the fold under "|| true" so nobody saw it
evidence: trace-store.test.mjs "a trace that cannot be cleaned is named and the rest are still cleaned"

what: The scorecard names a left-behind trace on the card it carries but does not price its rows
why: A crash between the insert and the delete can leave the rows in the archive as well, so pricing both places would count the card's cost twice
evidence: scorecard.test.mjs "a trace a failed cleanup left behind is named on the card it carries" expects [1000] tokens, not [1000, 77]

what: A trace parked in traces-hold/ is moved back by hand, not picked up by the fold
why: The card says moving it back makes it part of the next fold, and a 19.4 GB read-only fold can outrun the launcher's 60 s timeout
evidence: the 31 Oct trace folded in 2.09 s once the code was read-only; nothing in trace-store.mjs looks in traces-hold

what: status prunes no record it reads
why: Asking what is left behind must never be the reason a cleanup fails, so status stays read-only and filters left-behind.json against the files that are actually on disk
evidence: trace-store.mjs status(); trace-store.mjs comment above the filter
